analysis: To determine which drugs cause hypokalemia, we analyze each option based on established pharmacological effects. Amphotericin B is known to cause renal potassium loss, leading to hypokalemia. Insulin drives potassium into cells, which can also result in decreased serum potassium levels. Carbenoxolone has been associated with increased potassium excretion, contributing to hypokalemia. Cyclosporine's effect on potassium is less clear, with some evidence suggesting it may not directly cause hypokalemia. NSAIDs typically do not cause hypokalemia; they are more likely to lead to hyperkalemia due to their effects on renal blood flow.
